newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ekran says no Bakun rights issue.
newsitem.headline: Ekran says no Bakun rights issue.

text.p: Ekran Bhd, the main developer of the Bakun hydroelectric dam, does not expect to conduct a rights issue for the Bakun operating company in the near future, Ekran's chairman said on Wednesday.
Bakun Hydro-Electric Corp Bhd, the operator of the $6.2 billion dam, was expected to do a one-for-one rights issue next year.
Ting said the company was not planning any rights issue for Bakun one or two years down the line as planned earlier. "We will use other instruments," he said, without giving details.

Ekran recently completed a poorly-received rights issue of 257.1 million shares, which was undersubscribed by 62.77 percent. The results forced Ting to pick up over 90 percent of the unwanted portion for 859.8 million ringgit.

Ekran had offered the 257.1 million one-for-one rights issue at 5.70 ringgit a piece. Ting's purchase of the additional shares boosted the stake held in Ekran by him and his wife to 55.7 percent from 26.3 percent.
Ting said he was not disappointed by the performance of the rights issue and that the offering has been fully paid for.
"The 1.47 billion (ringgit) is already in the account of Ekran in the bank," Ting said.
Asked how he had funded the rights issue purchase which totalled about 1.2 billion ringgit, he said, "It is rude to ask the question...do I look like I don't have money.
Analysts had speculated Ting might restructure his holdings in Ekran-related companies or seek bank loans to finance the rights purchase.

Discussing the Bakun dam company listing, in which Ekran will be the biggest shareholder with a 32 percent stake, Ting said, "We will release the prospectus (of the Bakun issue) by the end of this month."
The stock of the dam, which is being built in the rainforests of eastern Sarawak state, is scheduled to be listed on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange in August.

Commenting on news reports that he may restructure Ekran in a plan involving other group companies, Ting said, "I will announce it when the time comes, when the approval is received from the authorities."
He did not elaborate on the restructuring plan, and declined comment on rumours that he was planning to sell his stakes in Ekran-related firms to Ekran.
Ting is a controlling shareholder in Granite Industries Bhd, PWE Industries Bhd, Wembley Industries Holdings Bhd and Pacific Chemicals Bhd.
He said a 13-member board has been constituted for the Bakun Hydroelectric Corp Bhd had been constituted, with him as the chairman.

Ekran has seven directors on the board of Bakun, including Ting. The Finance Ministry, the Sarawak state government, Khazanah Nasional Bhd, the Sarawak Electricity Supply Corp, Tenaga Nasional and the Employees Provident Fund, each have one representative.
"The undersubscription (was) due to market, rumours and negative views of people," Ting said, when asked about the performance of the Ekran rights issue.

He said the media and analysts with research houses have held a very negative view of the Bakun dam project. "They don't have a positive view .... that Bakun has great potential in the future," he said.
"Ekran is looking for long-term investment, that is why we are taking up 960 million ringgit worth of equity (in Bakun)," Ting said.
He said Ekran would diversify into some smaller businesses "to keep the income coming" while Bakun dam was under construction.
The 15.5 billion ringgit dam, which will produce 2,400 MW of power, is scheduled for completion in the year 2003.
"We will stick to what group businesses we have at the moment," he said, when asked to elaborate.
"One of them is expanding SAEGA Airlines," he added.
-- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-201 4813)
